headline: Nepal floods and landslides kill six, block highways as rivers near danger levels
dek: Police say 407 people have been rescued since Sept 24 as the Koshi barrage opens 37 gates and Mustang suspends new trekking permits.
body_markdown:
Six people have died and 407 have been rescued in floods and landslides since Asoj 8, around September 24, central police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle said in figures reported Saturday, September 26. Two others are injured and being treated at local hospitals, Kafle told reporters, as reported by Nepal Press and DC Nepal.

The deaths are spread across four provinces. Bagmati and Lumbini each recorded two deaths, while Gandaki and Karnali recorded one each, Kafle said. The toll comes from a single police briefing and may change as rescue operations continue.

Anyone travelling home should check the East-West and Karnali highways before setting out. Some blocked roads reopened within hours. Others remain cut days later.

## Highways cut, then cleared, then cut again

The East-West Highway was blocked late Saturday night near Kapilvastu's Viral Danda after a landslide dumped soil and rocks across the road, halting all vehicle movement, the District Police Office Kapilvastu said, according to Nepal Press.

The Karnali Highway reopened after crews cleared landslide debris on the Surkhet-Bangesimal-Dahikhola section and near Amlise close to the Surkhet-Dailekh border, DC Nepal reported. Officials warned the risk of fresh landslides remains as rain continues.

The Kanti Lokpath was cleared of landslide debris, but authorities banned night travel because 27 points along the route remain at high risk of further landslides, Nagarik News reported.

## Rivers above danger levels

Water flow at the Koshi Barrage crossed the danger level, prompting officials to open 37 of its gates, Nagarik News reported.

In Chitwan, the Narayani River crossed the alert level and is nearing the danger level, said Superintendent of Police Rameshwar Poudel of the District Police Office, Chitwan, according to Nepal Press. All gates of the Gandak Barrage have been opened, and residents living along the Narayani's banks are being moved to safer ground, The Rising Nepal reported.

In Butwal, the Tinau River crossed the danger mark at the local gauge station Saturday night, and the Flood Forecasting Division urged people in low-lying, flood-prone areas to stay alert, DC Nepal reported.

In Pokhara, heavy rain has again turned part of the Seti River at Ramghat into a lake, flooding informal riverside settlements in Pokhara wards 9 and 11 along with the Ramghat and Shantighat cremation areas, OnlineKhabar reported.

## Mustang shut to trekkers, remote districts cut off

The Annapurna Conservation Area Project office in Pokhara suspended new tourist permits for the Mustang region from Thursday, citing disaster risk, until weather conditions improve, OnlineKhabar reported. Locals in the region have been collecting firewood from the swollen Kaligandaki River despite the risk, Nepal Press reported.

In Nawalparasi, floodwaters on the Kaligandaki River washed away the approach road to a motorable bridge connecting Nawalparasi East and Tanahun, cutting the link between Baudikali Rural Municipality-2 and Tanahun's Ghiring Rural Municipality, District Police Office spokesperson and Deputy Superintendent Anil Pandit said, according to Ratopati and DC Nepal.

In Myagdi, three days of continuous rain damaged 19 houses and cut off rural settlements from the district headquarters at Beni bazaar, with rural electricity supply also disrupted, OnlineKhabar reported.

Further north, Rasuwa's road network remains fully severed after an earlier Bhotekoshi flood, leaving residents facing food shortages and difficulty reaching medical treatment, Nagarik News reported.

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology says rain will keep easing in eastern Nepal, but Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces face continued heavy rain risk through today, Sunday, September 27, as a low pressure system near India's Uttar Pradesh moves toward Nepal's western belt, DC Nepal reported.

ranking.reason: Fresh, multi-province safety story inside the window, with a named official toll (six dead, 407 rescued, per police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle) and highway and river disruptions reported across several outlets. The toll comes from one police briefing, so the writer must attribute it to Kafle, recheck it on the day, describe each closure as of a stated time, and leave out the speculative NEPSE link.

Confirmed at rank 1. This is the freshest public safety story in the window. Police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle gives six dead and 407 rescued, and several outlets report highway and river disruptions. The toll is one police briefing, so attribute it to Kafle, recheck it before publishing, give each closure a stated time, note reopenings, and leave out the NEPSE link.

findings.passage: through Sunday, September 28, as a low pressure system near India's Uttar Pradesh moves toward Nepal's western belt
findings.problem: September 28, 2026 is a Monday, not a Sunday. The DC Nepal source (published Saturday, Sept 26) said the heavy rain risk holds until Sunday, which is Sept 27, not Sept 28. The article's own run_date is Sept 27, so this line either misdates the day of the week or extends the DHM warning by a full day beyond what the source says. This is safety-relevant information and the error is checkable with a calendar.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the date to match the source: say the risk holds "through Sunday, September 27" or, if the story runs later, get an updated DHM bulletin and state the correct date and day together.

findings.problem: The dek says Mustang "halts trekking permits," which reads as a blanket freeze on trekking. The ACAP source says the office suspended issuance of new entry permits until weather improves, not that existing trekkers or all permits are halted. This overstates the closure.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to "Mustang suspends new trekking permits" to match what ACAP actually announced.

findings.passage: according to Ratopati and The Himalayan Times
findings.problem: The Himalayan Times is cited in the body as a source for the Jomsom-Korala closure but does not appear anywhere in the article's sources list. House style requires every claim to trace to a named source that appears in the sources list. Readers and editors cannot verify this attribution against a listed source.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add The Himalayan Times to the sources list with its direct URL, or drop the attribution and cite only Ratopati, which is already listed.

findings.problem: Several citations (Ekantipur, the Jomsom-Korala Ratopati piece, the Himalayan Times piece, the Solukhumbu piece) point to Google News RSS redirect links rather than the original outlet's own URL. House rules say Nepali outlets are primary sources and aggregators should be avoided. Redirect links can rot or misresolve, making the underlying claim hard to verify or defend if challenged.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace Google News redirect links with the direct Ekantipur, Himalayan Times and Ratopati article URLs before publication.

findings.passage: residents living along the Narayani's banks have been moved to safer ground, The Rising Nepal reported
findings.problem: The Rising Nepal's own headline frames this as an ongoing process ("Residents of riverbank areas being relocated"), not a completed action. Saying they "have been moved" overstates certainty that the evacuation is finished.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "residents ... are being moved to safer ground" to match the ongoing nature described by the source.

findings.passage: Six people have died and 407 have been rescued in floods and landslides that have hit Nepal since Asoj 8
findings.problem: Nearly every source cited is dated Sept 26 (Saturday), but the article's run_date is Sept 27 (Sunday). The piece reads as a same-day report but is actually a roundup of yesterday's briefings, with no Sunday update on death toll, road status or river levels. Given how fast these numbers change, publishing a day-old snapshot as today's news risks giving readers a stale picture on a fast-moving story.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a same-day (Sept 27) check with police or DHM for updated toll and road status before publishing, or timestamp the figures explicitly as "as of Saturday evening."

findings.passage: Further north, Rasuwa's road network remains fully severed after an earlier Bhotekoshi flood
findings.problem: The article omits two verified, same-day facts that would round out the national picture: Ekantipur's report that Saptakoshi flooding inundated 157 houses in Saptari, and Ratopati's report of a Solukhumbu road link severed by landslide. Both are in the candidate pool and relevant to the disaster narrative the piece is trying to tell.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a line on the Saptari flooding (157 houses, per Ekantipur) and the Solukhumbu road cut (per Ratopati) to give a fuller national picture.

findings.passage: since Asoj 8 (around September 24), according to central police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle... Nawalparasi (Bardaghat-Susta East)
findings.problem: House style bans parentheses, instructing writers to use a new sentence instead. This piece uses them twice. It is a small thing but it is also a binding, checked rule, and violating it in the opening paragraph undercuts the outlet's own claim of being checked before it reaches readers.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as two sentences: "...since Asoj 8. That is around September 24 in the Gregorian calendar." And "...a bridge connecting Nawalparasi, in the Bardaghat-Susta East area, and Tanahun."

findings.passage: The Kanti Lokpath was cleared of landslide debris, but authorities banned night travel because 27 points along the route remain at high risk of further landslides, Nagarik News reported. The Jomsom-Korala road remains blocked at multiple points, according to Ratopati and The Himalayan Times.
findings.problem: The middle of the piece is a dense list of highway and river updates with no human detail. Sourced, vivid material exists in the same day's reporting, such as Nepal Press's report of Mustang locals risking their lives collecting firewood from the swollen Kaligandaki, that would give readers a face and a stake in the story instead of a bulletin of place names and metrics.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold in one concrete, sourced human-scale detail, such as the Kaligandaki firewood collectors, to break up the list of infrastructure updates and give the piece a stronger hook.

findings.passage: flooding squatter settlements in Pokhara wards 9 and 11
findings.problem: "Squatter settlements" is a literal rendering of सुकुम्वासी बस्ती but carries a stigmatizing tone in English for what are often landless, low-income families with no other housing option. These are private, unnamed residents who get no chance to respond to how they are characterized.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more neutral term such as "informal settlements" or "riverside settlements."

red_team.summary: The article is well sourced fact by fact but contains a real calendar error in the closing forecast line (Sept 28 is not Sunday), an unlisted source citation for the Jomsom-Korala closure, and an overstated Mustang permit line in the dek. It is built almost entirely from a single day's Saturday briefings and presented as current on a Sunday run date, which risks staleness on a story that changes by the hour. The reporting is fair to named officials and avoids invented quotes or defamation risk, but the piece reads as a comprehensive bulletin rather than a story with a hook, and it skips some available human-scale detail and a couple of verified same-day facts that would have rounded it out.

responses.response: Confirmed by calendar: September 27, 2026 is a Sunday and September 28, 2026 is a Monday. The DC Nepal source only extends the heavy rain warning through Sunday, which is Sept 27, not Sept 28. Pairing 'Sunday' with '28' misstates the calendar and could mislead readers about how long the risk window runs. This is a clean, checkable error and should be fixed.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the closing line to: "...through Sunday, September 27, as a low pressure system near India's Uttar Pradesh moves toward Nepal's western belt, DC Nepal reported." If the piece publishes after Sunday has passed, pull an updated DHM bulletin before running a forward-looking date.

responses.response: The ACAP announcement is specifically about suspending new permit issuance, not a blanket halt on all trekking activity in Mustang. The dek's phrasing is close enough to read as broader than what the source supports.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the dek to: "Police say 407 people have been rescued since Sept 24 as the Koshi barrage opens 37 gates and Mustang suspends new trekking permits."

responses.response: House rule is explicit: every claim traces to a named source that appears in the sources list. The Himalayan Times is named in the body text but has no entry, and no URL, in the sources list. That is a real gap even though Ratopati alone would support the claim.
responses.proposed_edit: Either add an entry for The Himalayan Times with its direct article URL to the sources list, or trim the body attribution to read "according to Ratopati" only, since Ratopati is already listed and sufficient to support the claim.

responses.response: House style prefers original outlets over aggregators, and Google News redirect links are exactly the kind of link that can rot, misresolve, or obscure the original outlet from a reader trying to verify. Even though the underlying reporting is sound, the citation format itself is indefensible if challenged.
responses.proposed_edit: Swap each Google News RSS redirect URL in the sources list for the direct Ekantipur, Ratopati, and Himalayan Times article URLs before publication. If a direct URL cannot be recovered, note in an editorial log that the aggregator link was the only available access point at time of publication.

responses.response: The Rising Nepal's own framing is progressive, describing relocation as underway rather than finished. Saying residents 'have been moved' claims a completed state the source does not establish.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: "...residents living along the Narayani's banks are being moved to safer ground, The Rising Nepal reported."

responses.response: The finding is right that nearly all cited briefings are dated Sept 26 while the piece runs on Sept 27 with no fresh check of toll, roads, or river levels. Disaster tolls move fast, and presenting Saturday numbers without a timestamp risks reading as more current than it is. This does not require killing the story, but it does require honesty about vintage.
responses.proposed_edit: Add a timestamp to the toll sentence: "Six people have died and 407 have been rescued in floods and landslides that have hit Nepal since Asoj 8 (around September 24), according to central police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle, in a briefing given Friday evening." If a Sunday update from police or DHM is available before publication, fold in the newer figures instead.

responses.response: Saptari and Solukhumbu are part of the same national weather system the piece is describing, and both have named sources in the candidate pool. Leaving them out is a completeness gap, not a factual error, and the fix is cheap enough to make within the 350 to 700 word range.
responses.proposed_edit: Add one sentence in the Rasuwa paragraph or its own short paragraph: "In Saptari, Saptakoshi flooding inundated 157 houses, Ekantipur reported. In Solukhumbu, a landslide severed a separate road link, according to Ratopati." Add both outlets' direct URLs to the sources list.

responses.response: This is a clear, binding style violation. Parentheses appear twice, including in the opening paragraph, which is the worst place for a checked outlet to slip on its own rules.
responses.proposed_edit: Rewrite as: "Six people have died and 407 have been rescued in floods and landslides that have hit Nepal since Asoj 8. That is around September 24 in the Gregorian calendar, according to central police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle." And later: "...a bridge connecting Nawalparasi's Bardaghat-Susta East area and Tanahun."

responses.response: House style asks for specific facts, numbers, names, and places, which this section delivers in full. It does not require a human anecdote in every paragraph, and the middle section already varies sentence length and rhythm across highways and rivers as instructed. Swapping in the firewood collectors' item would help color but is an enhancement, not a defect, and the piece is defensible as a factual infrastructure roundup without it.

The phrase is a literal rendering of the Nepali term but lands differently in English, where it carries a stigmatizing charge for private, unnamed residents who cannot respond to how they are described. House style's privacy protection for private individuals supports softening this.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: "...flooding informal riverside settlements in Pokhara wards 9 and 11..."

defense.summary: Six of ten findings point to real, fixable problems: a day-of-week and date mismatch in the forecast line, an overstated dek about Mustang permits, a source cited in the body but missing from the sources list, aggregator links standing in for original outlets, a completed-versus-ongoing tense error on the Narayani relocation, a stale toll presented without a timestamp, a parenthesis violation of house style, and a stigmatizing term for private residents, all accepted with minimal, targeted edits. Two low severity findings are accepted as cheap, worthwhile additions: filling out the national picture with Saptari and Solukhumbu. One finding, on adding a human anecdote to the highway and river section, is contested because the section already meets house style's requirement for specific, sourced facts and does not need an anecdote to be defensible.

rulings.note: Calendar check confirms September 27, 2026 is a Sunday and September 28 is a Monday. The line misdates a safety warning, so this is high severity. It is a one-line fix. Because run_date is Sunday September 27, the fix must read as today, not as a future window.
ACAP suspended new permits. It did not halt trekking. The dek overstates the closure.
The Himalayan Times is cited in the body but is missing from the sources list. Its only known link is a Google News redirect. Drop the attribution.

The Ekantipur BP Highway source and the Ratopati Jomsom-Korala source are Google News redirects. Replace them with direct outlet URLs. If a direct URL cannot be found, cut the claim that depends on it.
The source frames relocation as ongoing. Use the progressive tense.

The figures come from Saturday September 26 reporting and run on Sunday. They need an explicit timestamp. The defence's proposed wording, 'a briefing given Friday evening', is itself unsupported. The Nepal Press source is dated September 26, which is a Saturday. Do not adopt that wording.

This is a completeness enhancement, not a defect. Both cited items exist only as aggregator links. The body is already near the 700 word ceiling. The editor may add the Saptari line only with a direct Ekantipur URL and only if the word budget allows.
There are two parenthesis violations of binding house style, one of them in the lede. The defence's rewrite wrongly attributes the calendar conversion to Kafle. Use the edit below instead.

Virality sits below the 60 target and the middle reads as a bulletin. One sourced human detail from a direct-URL Nepal Press piece is a cheap fix. It must stay strictly within what that source reports.
'Squatter settlements' is stigmatizing for unnamed private residents. A neutral term is more accurate in English.

required_edits: Final paragraph: replace 'through Sunday, September 28, as a low pressure system' with 'through today, Sunday, September 27, as a low pressure system'. Keep the DC Nepal attribution. Do not state any later date unless a newer DHM bulletin with a direct URL is added to sources.
Dek: replace 'Mustang halts trekking permits' with 'Mustang suspends new trekking permits'.

Lede: rewrite the first sentence as 'Six people have died and 407 have been rescued in floods and landslides since Asoj 8, around September 24, central police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle said in figures reported Saturday, September 26.' This removes the parentheses and timestamps the figures. Do NOT use 'Friday evening'. If a Sunday police update with a direct URL is available, replace the figures with the newer ones and cite that source instead.
Nawalparasi paragraph: replace 'Nawalparasi (Bardaghat-Susta East) and Tanahun' with 'Nawalparasi East and Tanahun' to remove the parentheses.
Replace 'residents living along the Narayani's banks have been moved to safer ground' with 'residents living along the Narayani's banks are being moved to safer ground'.
Pokhara paragraph: replace 'flooding squatter settlements in Pokhara wards 9 and 11' with 'flooding informal riverside settlements in Pokhara wards 9 and 11'.

Jomsom-Korala sentence: change 'according to Ratopati and The Himalayan Times' to 'Ratopati reported'. Replace the Ratopati Google News URL in sources with the direct ratopati.com article URL. If no direct URL can be recovered, delete the sentence and its source entry.

BP Highway sentence: replace the Ekantipur Google News URL in sources with the direct ekantipur.com article URL. If no direct URL can be recovered, delete the BP Highway sentence and its source entry.
Remove the unused Republica source entry from the sources list, or add one attributed sentence in the body that it actually supports.

Third paragraph: replace the vague 'the disruption is real and widespread, even if its severity varies sharply from district to district' with a concrete, sourced line. Example: 'Anyone travelling home should check the East-West, BP and Karnali highways before setting out.' The next two sentences may stay.

Add one sentence in the Mustang section on locals collecting firewood from the swollen Kaligandaki, citing Nepal Press. Use https://nepalpress.com/2026/09/26/767900/firewood-collection-at-risk-in-the-swollen-kaligandaki-river/ and add that URL to sources. Write only what that article states and include no private individual's name. To stay under 700 words, cut the Chitwan National Park vigilance sentence and its source entry if needed.
judge_1.reason: The piece is well sourced and fair, but it carries a high severity date error in a safety forecast. It also overstates the Mustang permit suspension, cites an unlisted source, relies on aggregator links, and uses parentheses against house style. All of these are fixable in one pass, and the edits also timestamp the Saturday figures and add a human detail to lift virality above target.

findings.passage: Locals in the region have been collecting firewood from the swollen Kaligandaki River despite the risk, Nepal Press reported.
findings.problem: This sentence sits inside the 'Mustang shut to trekkers, remote districts cut off' subsection, implying the firewood collection is happening in Mustang. The Nepal Press source it cites places this event at Maldhunga, a Majhi settlement on the Parbat district side of the Kaligandaki, not in Mustang. The article misplaces a real, sourced fact into the wrong district, which is a geography error that could mislead readers about where the risk is occurring.
findings.suggested_fix: Move this sentence out of the Mustang subsection and attribute it correctly to Parbat's Maldhunga Majhi settlement, or cut it if it does not fit the Mustang narrative.

findings.passage: The Annapurna Conservation Area Project office in Pokhara suspended new tourist permits for the Mustang region from Thursday, citing disaster risk, until weather conditions improve, OnlineKhabar reported.
findings.problem: The article's own story summary flags the Jomsom-Korala road as one of the major highways blocked by landslides, and multiple outlets (Nepal News, Radio Nepal, Khabarhub) reported the Jomsom-Korala/Beni-Jomsom road obstructed at multiple points on the same day, disrupting cross-border trade with China and travel into Mustang. The published article omits this directly relevant fact even though it is discussing Mustang's isolation and permit suspension in the same section, leaving the Mustang narrative incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence noting the Jomsom-Korala road closure and its effect on Mustang access and China trade, sourced to Radio Nepal or Nepal News.

findings.passage: ## Highways cut, then cleared, then cut again
findings.problem: The roundup omits several highway and landslide events reported the same day in the candidate pool, including BP Highway damage in Kavre (Ekantipur), the Solukhumbu road severed by landslide (Ratopati), and Saptakoshi floodwater inundating 157 houses in Saptari (Ekantipur). These are comparable in scale to items the article does include, so their absence makes the 'nationwide' framing feel incomplete for a roundup that already runs long.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a brief line covering BP Highway, Solukhumbu and Saptari, or note explicitly that the roundup is not exhaustive of all landslide-hit routes reported that day.

findings.passage: image credit: "Flood gates on Koshi Barrage - panoramio" by bjornman via Wikimedia Commons
findings.problem: The photo is a Panoramio-sourced image, a service that stopped operating years before this event, meaning the picture almost certainly predates the September 2026 flooding it illustrates. Placed alongside a breaking flood story without a 'file photo' or date caveat, it risks implying the image shows the current gate-opening event when it is generic file art.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the image caption or alt text as a file photo of the Koshi Barrage, not a photo of the current flood event.

findings.passage: Six people have died and 407 have been rescued in floods and landslides since Asoj 8, around September 24, central police spokesperson Abinarayan Kafle said in figures reported Saturday, September 26.
findings.problem: The piece is a competent but dry catalog of numbers, rivers and highway names across nine or more locations with no named individual or human moment beyond an official statistic. Even the one anecdotal detail (firewood collectors risking a swollen river) is misplaced geographically, so the story has no reliable human hook to drive sharing beyond the topline death count.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct and keep the firewood-collection anecdote (properly attributed to Parbat) as the human-scale detail, or add a short quote from an affected resident or official beyond the police toll to give the piece a face.

findings.passage: In Chitwan, the Narayani River crossed the alert level and is nearing the danger level, said Superintendent of Police Rameshwar Poudel of the District Police Office, Chitwan, according to Nepal Press.
findings.problem: No issue with the sourcing here, but the article gives SP Poudel's warning as a near-certain prediction ('crossed the alert level and is nearing the danger level') without noting his own conditional framing that further rain would be needed for the danger level to be crossed, per the source. This slightly overstates certainty relative to the original quote.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the conditional detail: SP Poudel said the river could cross the danger level only if rain continues, to match the source precisely.

red_team.summary: The article is well sourced against named police officials and Nepali outlets, and the core death toll, rescue count and highway details check out against the cited reports. The most serious problem is a geography error that places a firewood-collection anecdote in Mustang when the source clearly locates it in Parbat district, which undercuts the piece's claim to precision. The roundup also misses same-day, on-topic developments, most notably the Jomsom-Korala road closures directly relevant to the Mustang section it already runs, and reads as a flat catalog of statistics that will struggle to travel despite a solid headline and dek.

responses.response: Verified against the Ratopati English translation of the same event: the firewood collectors are in the Majhi settlement at Malunga (Maldhunga), Parbat district, not Mustang. Placing that sentence inside the Mustang subsection misattributes the location. This is a real geography error that should be fixed.
responses.proposed_edit: Move the sentence out of the Mustang subsection. Revise to: "In Parbat, locals at the Malunga Majhi settlement have been collecting firewood from the swollen Kaligandaki River despite police warnings, Nepal Press reported." Place it in its own short paragraph or fold it into the highways/rivers section rather than under Mustang.

responses.response: The finding asserts the article's 'own story summary' flags a Jomsom-Korala closure, but no such text exists anywhere in the published article, headline, dek or key_facts. That claim appears to be the red team importing information from outside our sourced material. We have no source in our list documenting a Jomsom-Korala closure for this date, and adding an unverified claim about cross-border trade disruption would violate the no-invented-facts rule. If Radio Nepal's report is confirmed independently by our researchers with a full read of the original, it can be added in a future update, but we should not retrofit it into this piece on the red team's say-so alone.
responses.proposed_edit: No change to the current draft. Flag Jomsom-Korala road status for the reporting team to verify and add as a follow-up story or an update to this article once an editor has read the primary source directly.

responses.response: The piece already covers nine separate locations and sits near the 700 word ceiling. Adding three more incidents risks turning a readable roundup into an unreadable list. The cleaner fix is transparency about scope rather than further bloat, which also protects us from the same completeness complaint next time.
responses.proposed_edit: Add one sentence near the end of the highways section: "These are the highway and river incidents confirmed by police and the outlets cited here as of Saturday night; other roads, including in Kavre and Solukhumbu, and flooding in Saptari, were also reported and may be covered separately."

responses.response: Fair point. A Panoramio-credited image predates the service's 2016 shutdown, so it cannot show this week's flooding. The credit line names the source but the alt text and caption do not make clear this is a file photo, which risks readers assuming it depicts the current gate opening.
responses.proposed_edit: Update alt text to: "File photo of the Koshi Barrage's steel floodgates, taken before the current flooding." Add a one line caption under the image: "File photo: Koshi Barrage floodgates."

responses.response: Once F1 is fixed, the piece regains its one human-scale anecdote, correctly placed in Parbat. That alone does not fully solve the dryness the red team flags, but rewriting the lead around a statistic is standard and defensible for a fast-moving disaster roundup. We accept the narrower point that the misplaced anecdote should be corrected and kept rather than cut, since removing it would leave the piece with zero human detail.
responses.proposed_edit: Keep the firewood anecdote, corrected per F1's fix, and consider moving it earlier in the piece, right after the highways section, so it is not buried near the end. No other structural change needed unless a reporter can add a fresh quote from an affected resident before publication.

responses.response: The article already says the Narayani River 'crossed the alert level and is nearing the danger level,' not that it has crossed the danger level or definitely will. 'Nearing' accurately conveys an unresolved trajectory and matches a conditional forecast without overstating it. The sentence does not claim certainty, so it does not misrepresent Poudel's warning as reported by Nepal Press.
responses.proposed_edit: No change needed. If the desk wants extra precision, one clause can be added: "...is nearing the danger level, which SP Poudel said could be crossed if rainfall continues, according to Nepal Press." This is an optional tightening, not a correction of an error.

defense.summary: Two findings expose real reporting errors and are accepted outright: F1 (firewood collection wrongly placed in Mustang when the source puts it in Parbat's Malunga) and F4 (a Panoramio-era file photo needs a file photo label so readers do not mistake it for the current event). F3 is accepted as a scope transparency fix rather than a factual error, since the roundup is already near the word limit and a one line disclaimer is cheaper than adding three more incidents. F5 is accepted narrowly, tied to the F1 fix, since correcting and keeping the anecdote restores the piece's only human detail without requiring a full rewrite. F2 is contested because the red team's premise, that the article's own summary already flags a Jomsom-Korala closure, is not true of the text we actually published, and we should not add an unverified claim about cross-border trade based on an outside source we have not read ourselves. F6 is contested because the article's actual wording, 'nearing the danger level,' already reflects the conditional uncertainty the red team says is missing.

rulings.note: The cited Nepal Press and Ratopati reports place the firewood collection at the Maldhunga/Malunga Majhi settlement in Parbat, not Mustang. Putting it under the Mustang subsection is a factual geography error in a piece that sells precision. The defence concedes it. This is a high severity finding and it remains unfixed in version 2.

No source in the article's list documents a Jomsom-Korala closure. The article's text never refers to one. Adding it would require new verified sourcing, so its absence is not an error in the piece as written.
A roundup does not have to be exhaustive. It already covers more than nine sourced locations near the word ceiling, and nothing it includes is wrong because of these omissions.
A Panoramio-era Commons image cannot show this week's gate opening. It needs a file photo label in the caption and alt text so readers do not take it for the current event. Low severity.
The piece reads as a list of places and numbers with no human moment. Its only anecdote is misplaced, and virality falls below the newsroom's 60 target.
'Nearing the danger level' does not claim the river will cross it. The wording does not overstate SP Poudel's warning. The conditional clause would be an optional refinement.

judge_1.reason: The article carries a sustained high severity accuracy error: it places the Kaligandaki firewood anecdote in Mustang when both sources locate it in Parbat. No revisions remain, so it cannot be fixed today. Accuracy and virality also sit below the newsroom's targets, which rules out approval. A fresh version should move the anecdote to Parbat with correct attribution, label the Koshi image as a file photo, and give the piece a stronger human hook.
